newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan court says woman may marry man of choice.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan court says woman may marry man of choice.

text.p: A Pakistani court freed a woman to join her husband on Monday, dismissing her militant Moslem father's petition that their marriage was invalid because it had taken place without his permission.

"Marriage without the consent of a wali (guardian) is not invalid," said Justice Ehsan ul-Haq Chaudhry, reading the Lahore High Court decision that settled what was seen as a test case pitting Moslem conservatives against women's rights advocates.
The three-member bench split 2-1 in a majority decision that allows Saima Waheed to leave a women's shelter where she has been kept under court order for the past 11 months.
"It's a historic decision for the women of Pakistan," said Asma Jahangir, Saima's lawyer and chairperson of the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan.

"It is the most wonderful day of my life," Saima's husband Arshad Ahmad, a college lecturer, said at the court. "We have gone through a great ordeal that was spread over 11 months. But now I can join hands with my wife once again. I am extremely happy.
Saima's father Abdul Waheed Ropri and his followers left the court-room silently after the decision, on which Ropri refused to comment. "There's no use in talking now," he said.
